# Incident Report — MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** | Source of all malicious traffic; consistent across DNS, HTTP, TLS, ARP |
| MAC | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183` maps to this MAC |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (workgroup/computer name `NEMOTODES`, joined to AD domain `nemotoads.health`, DC `NEMOTODE-DC` at 10.11.26.3) | NBNS name registrations from 10.11.26.183; SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp...nemotoads.health` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3) |

LAN scope: 10.11.26.0/24, gateway 10.11.26.1 (MAC 00:17:e0:b8:29:5e), domain controller 10.11.26.3 (MAC 00:24:e8:7f:09:5d).

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Suricata/ET alerts fired directly on the C2 traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, and `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`. This is corroborated behaviorally: the HTTP client `User-Agent` is literally `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the POST bodies exchanged with the C2 use the RAT's native protocol tokens `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1`, and `CMD=ENCD ... DATA=<encrypted blob>` (recovered via `tshark --export-objects http`).

## Delivery Chain
Traced via DNS/HTTP/TLS SNI in the minute before infection (04:50:10–04:50:16 UTC):

1. `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) — lure/landing page
2. `confirmsubscription.com` — redirector/click-through
3. `modandcrackedapk.com` → resolved to **193.42.38.139**, flagged by ET as a `ZPHP Domain` in both DNS lookup and TLS SNI — the fake cracked-software/APK download site that delivered the payload over TLS (payload contents not recoverable, session is encrypted).

Shortly after, the infected host began beaconing to the NetSupport RAT C2, and also called `geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (104.26.1.231) — the RAT's built-in vendor geolocation lookup, benign infrastructure context rather than an indicator itself.

## Command-and-Control
- **C2 endpoint: 194.180.191.64:443** — plaintext HTTP (not TLS, despite the port) POST requests to `/fakeurl.htm`, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, beaconing roughly every 60 seconds from 08:50:45 through at least 09:43:29 (local capture time, +0400). First check-in body: `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1`; later exchanges use `CMD=ENCD` with encrypted `DATA=` payloads — the RAT's data-exchange phase.

## Indicators of Compromise (grounded in this capture)
